title: Redlines Comparison (JSON v2)
description: Schema for redlines.comparison.Comparison.to_dict() -- the M2 comparison document: two block trees, what corresponds between them, and what changed (ADR-0032, ADR-0033). Frozen at schema_version 2.0. Policy: an additive change (a new optional field, a new change kind, a new statistic) bumps the minor and widens this same file; a breaking change bumps the major, gets its own ADR, and the previous major stays producible from its own schema file. This one file also carries the block tree, at #/definitions/blockTree -- there is no separate block-tree schema -- because a second file would need a cross-file $ref to a URL that does not exist until this file itself is published (M4), which is a resolution trap offline and in tests. The presence of the schema_version key is itself the v1/v2 discriminator: v1's Redlines.output_json has no such key at all.

schema_version.description: This file's own version, drift-tested against redlines.comparison.SCHEMA_VERSION.

source.description: The earlier document, byte-for-byte redlines.blocks.BlockTree.to_dict() output -- not reshaped, so an M1 expected tree stays valid as a slice of this document.

test.description: The later document, in the same shape as source.

changes.description: The change tree: a flat, document-ordered list of Change objects. The only nesting is a change's own inline ops; there are no child change nodes (ADR-0033).

alignment.description: OPTIONAL. Present only when the document was written with to_dict(include_alignment=True)/to_json(include_alignment=True). Every correspondence between the two trees, unchanged pairs included -- the whole set the change tree cannot express, because an unchanged pair produces no change node.

statistics.description: redlines.statistics.ComparisonStatistics.to_dict() (#139) -- always present, computed fresh from changes and both block trees rather than stored. Added after the initial JSON v2 freeze (#137); an additive, minor-version change (ADR-0011).

comparisonConfig.description: redlines.comparison.ComparisonConfig.to_dict() -- everything that decided what this comparison says (#135), so a reader can reproduce why two blocks were paired.

source_format.description: The format the source side was read as (e.g. 'markdown', 'text'), or 'blocks' if it arrived as an already-read block tree.

test_format.description: The same for the test side. A separate field because per-side detection means the two can legitimately differ.

profile.description: The structure profile both sides were read under, or '' when neither side was read (both arrived as block trees).

alignment.description: The AlignmentConfig in force, embedded whole -- one source of truth, so a new threshold is one edit.

similarity.description: The RESOLVED similarity backend that actually ran. config.alignment.similarity is what was asked for ('auto' by default); this is what 'auto' resolved to, or what was demanded.

processor.description: The leaf differ's type name, e.g. 'WholeDocumentProcessor'. A name, not a serialised object -- a custom RedlinesProcessor is supported (R17) and this is how the payload records that one was used.

budget_exhausted.description: Whether alignment's max_comparisons ran out. True means 'we stopped looking', not 'nothing more was there'.

filter.description: The redlines.filters.ChangeFilter that produced this comparison's changes, or null for an unfiltered comparison (#138). Added after the initial JSON v2 freeze (#137); an additive, minor-version change (ADR-0011).

passes.description: Which passes run, always in the fixed PASS_NAMES order regardless of the order a caller supplied.

similarity.description: The backend that was ASKED for. The RESOLVED backend that ran is recorded separately, at config.similarity and alignment.backend.

move_kinds.description: Which structural kinds the move pass may report. Container moves are not reported in 1.0; they surface as their children moving.

passName.description: redlines.alignment.PASS_NAMES -- a closed vocabulary naming the engine's own passes, not an open reader vocabulary.

dropped.description: What the reader did not carry across, one entry per kind (R3).

fallback_count.description: How many blocks matched no rule at all (derived; ADR-0030).

block.description: redlines.blocks.Block.to_dict() -- one node of the document tree.

text.description: The block's own text, label already stripped. Container blocks (document, section, table, row) normally leave this empty.

label.description: The document's own label for this block ('7.2', '(a)', 'Schedule 2'), or null.

path.description: The ADR-0029 address: '/' for the root, or '/kind[n]' segments repeated.

role.description: The optional semantic role (ADR-0005); open vocabulary, not enforced here.

matched_by.description: The rule that recognised this block (ADR-0030). Open reader vocabulary -- deliberately not closed, unlike the alignment pass names.

confidence.description: How sure the reader is (ADR-0030). Not rounded on the wire -- that rounding is reserved for alignment and change confidence (N1).

attrs.description: Reader-specific detail with no place in the core model. Shape is the reader's own; not constrained here.

span.description: redlines.blocks.Span.to_dict() -- a typed range of characters inside one block's own text.

type.description: An open span type (ADR-0005): e.g. defined_term, cross_reference, party, date, amount, citation.

value.description: What the span means where that differs from what it says, or null when the text speaks for itself.

dropped.description: redlines.blocks.Dropped.to_dict() -- one kind of content a reader did not carry into the tree (R3).

changeKind.description: redlines.changes.ChangeKind -- a closed set in 1.0 (ADR-0033). 'split' and 'merge' are reserved names nothing in 1.0 emits; adding them is a 1.1, minor-version change that widens this enum.

inlineKind.description: redlines.changes.InlineKind -- what one edit inside a block's text did.

change.description: redlines.changes.Change.to_dict() -- one thing that happened to one block. Every node carries both addresses, both labels and its inline ops regardless of which kind won under the move > renumber > modify precedence.

source_address.description: The block's address in the source tree, or null on an insert (the block is not in the source document).

test_address.description: The block's address in the test tree, or null on a delete.

role.description: Single-valued, from the test block, or the source block on a delete.

span_types.description: The types of spans this change TOUCHED -- sorted and deduplicated: for a modify, the span types on either side that overlap an inline op; for an insert/delete, every span type on the block. The values themselves are not copied here; they are on the blocks at these addresses.

matched_by.description: Which alignment pass found the pair, or 'unmatched' for an insert or a delete. This is alignment's own answer, not the reader's Block.matched_by (ADR-0030).

confidence.description: The alignment's confidence in the pair, rounded to 4 decimal places here and nowhere else (N1) -- 0.0 for an insert or a delete.

inline.description: The edits inside the text, in order. Empty on an insert or a delete.

breadcrumb.description: The ADR-0029 heading breadcrumb, test side (source side on a delete), outermost first.

inlineOp.description: redlines.changes.InlineOp.to_dict() -- one edit inside a block's text, in CHARACTER offsets into that block's own text (the same frame Span uses), never into the document.

source_text.description: The source run, '' for an insert. A slice of the source block's text, not a paraphrase (R27a).

test_text.description: The test run, '' for a delete.

alignment.description: redlines.alignment.Alignment.to_dict() -- what align() found: every pair, everything left over, and how.

pairs.description: Every correspondence, source document order, root first. Unchanged pairs are included.

inserted.description: Addresses of test blocks nothing matched, document order. Every one, not only the root of an inserted subtree.

deleted.description: Addresses of unmatched source blocks, likewise.

backend.description: The RESOLVED similarity backend that ran.

pass_counts.description: How many pairs each pass contributed, 'root' included and zeros present -- the evidence ADR-0008's review gate asks for.

alignedPair.description: redlines.alignment.AlignedPair.to_dict() -- one correspondence: this source block is that test block.

matched_by.description: Which pass found it, or 'root' for the root pair, which is given rather than found.

confidence.description: Rounded to 4 decimal places on the wire (N1).

moved.description: Whether the two blocks' parents fail to correspond, or the pair crosses its own siblings.

renumbered.description: Whether the parents correspond and the labels differ.

changeFilter.description: redlines.filters.ChangeFilter.to_dict() -- a declarative scope over a change tree (#138). An empty array field is no constraint; fields AND together, values within one field OR.

kinds.description: Keep only these change kinds. [] is no constraint.

address_prefixes.description: Keep only a change whose source_address or test_address sits at or under one of these, segment-aligned ('/section[1]' does not match '/section[11]'). [] is no constraint.

labels.description: Keep only a change whose source_label or test_label is one of these. [] is no constraint.

roles.description: Keep only a change whose role is one of these. [] is no constraint.

min_chars.description: Keep only a change whose max(chars_added, chars_deleted) is at least this many characters. 0 is no constraint.

has_inline.description: true keeps only a change with at least one inline op, false keeps only one with none, null is no constraint.

changeCounts.description: redlines.statistics.ChangeCounts.to_dict() -- how many changes there were, and what kind, over one list of change nodes (#139).

total.description: The sum of the five change-kind counts -- a count of change nodes, not blocks (a deleted 40-block schedule is one 'deleted').

tokens_changed.description: Tokens on both sides of every inline op, in the leaf differ's own units.

sectionStatistics.description: redlines.statistics.SectionStatistics.to_dict() -- counts and density for one section-with-heading unit: every block of kind 'section' that has a 'heading' child, wherever it sits in the tree. This is a deliberate reinterpretation of #139's 'top-level section' (see redlines/statistics.py's module docstring and the #138/#139/#140 PR body).

address.description: The section block's test address, or its source address when the whole section was deleted.

breadcrumb.description: The ADR-0029 heading breadcrumb leading to the section itself, outermost first.

blocks.description: How many blocks of the TEST tree have this section as their nearest enclosing one -- change-independent, from the unfiltered tree. 0 for a section deleted whole.

density.description: counts.total / blocks, rounded to 4 decimal places; 0.0 when blocks is 0.

counts.description: Every change in the comparison, tallied. Reflects a filtered change list when this comparison came from Comparison.filter().

sections.description: One row per section-with-heading unit that exists on either side, in document order.
